newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - May 16.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on May 16:

WASHINGTON - The Senate overwhelmingly rejected a White House-backed initiative to curtail late-term abortions that was offered as a way of derailing a Republican-sponsored bill banning the procedure.

WASHINGTON - The White House and GOP leaders finally put the finishing touches to a written summary of their budget deal, ending two weeks of acrimonious haggling over everything from tax cuts to Medicare changes.

WASHINGTON - After failing to achieve major improvements in District government operations over the past two years, the head of the D.C. financial control board says the answer may lie in a radical new approach that would strip Mayor Marion Barry of the power to run the city.
KINSHASA - Panic and confusion became the order of the day as rebel forces reportedly moved to within 25 miles of the capital and residents prepared for the city's expected fall.
BLACKSBURG, Va. - More than half this town's 37,000 residents are regular users of the Internet, making the community, on a per capita basis, one of the world's most wired places.

WASHINGTON - Presbyterian churches around the country are refusing to comply with a new church law that excludes gay men and women and anyone sexually active outside of marriage from ordained leadership positions in the church.
